pairs.difference: A: the two sneakers sit in a wide, low band across the middle-lower card, in 3/4 view, with the left toe close to the left edge (margin 0.033). The orange wall above is empty. B: the gift drum stands square to the camera, centered and symmetrical, with an even gap on every side (margin 0.123, above the real range). That is the lessons' generated framing: the whole object, centered, with a uniform border. A's empty top half is a weakness too, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Turn the gift box to a three-quarter angle and draw it bigger, so the bow nearly touches the top edge and one side comes close to the card edge. Don't leave an even border all around.

pairs.difference: B: the sunscreen bottle and sunglasses run off the bottom edge and nearly fill the height (0.856, margin 0.031), the way the real cards do. B matches the sunscreen card in the anchor sheet. A: the soccer ball sits centered and evenly inset (margin 0.144, above every real card), and a pitch line in the top-left corner pulls the eye away.
pairs.fix: Draw the soccer ball larger and lower so it is cut off by the bottom edge, fills about 85% of the card height and sits off-center. Remove the white field lines in the top corner.

pairs.difference: Both heroes are tilted on the diagonal. A: the parasol canopy sits in the upper left, and the lower-right quarter is left as empty argyle pattern (margin 0.095). B: the fan spreads across almost the whole width (0.86), and its top-right tip nearly reaches the edge. A's leftover empty corner is the only small hint, so this is close to a coin flip.
pairs.fix: Draw the parasol bigger and centered on the diagonal, so the canopy edge nearly touches the top-left edge and the hook handle nearly reaches the bottom-right corner.

pairs.difference: A: the fountain basin spans almost the full width (0.916), and the paving runs off the bottom and sides like real stage-floor cards. B: the cake stand stands straight on, centered and symmetrical, and covers only 0.242 of the card. Wide margins (0.121) leave purple wall and tablecloth around it, and the tablecloth takes up the bottom third.
pairs.fix: Draw the cake stand larger, turned to a three-quarter angle and slightly off-center. Its plates should almost touch the left and right edges, and less tablecloth should show.

pairs.difference: A: the mortarboard is a flat, wide shape centered in the rings. It is short (height 0.506, below the real range) and leaves empty bands of background above and below. B: the top hat is tilted, with its brim sweeping toward the right edge, and fills more of the height (0.625).
pairs.fix: Tilt the graduation cap toward the viewer, so the board shows as a diamond seen from above. Draw it bigger, filling about two-thirds of the card height, with the tassel hanging toward the bottom-right corner.

pairs.difference: A: the vending machine fills the height (0.79) and is turned to 3/4 view. B: the teacup and saucer are a short, wide shape (height 0.458, below the real range) floating mid-card. Wide margins (0.14) leave a large empty magenta gradient, and the steam wisp drifts into the top half as a faint second focus.
pairs.fix: Draw the teacup and saucer much larger, from a higher three-quarter angle, so the saucer nearly touches the left and right edges. Keep any steam small and close to the cup.

pairs.difference: B: the map is cut off by the top and right edges (margin 0.0), and the magnifier on top is the clear focal point, as on the real cropped cards. A: the pearl bracelet is a hollow ring with velvet showing through the middle, so it covers only 0.172 of the card (far below the real 0.233 minimum). At thumbnail size it reads as a thin outline on busy blue folds, with no solid mass to catch the eye.
pairs.fix: Show the pearl bracelet up close and tilted, with part of the strand piled up or draped so it reads as a solid mass. Let one side run past the card edge, and use a plain, simple background instead of wrinkled velvet.

pairs.difference: B: the scarf is tall and centered, filling the height (0.833) with the knot badge as the focal point. A: the red fan opens flat and horizontal through the middle. It is short (height 0.452, below the real range) and leaves wide empty bands of wavy blue above and below.
pairs.fix: Tilt the fan at a strong diagonal and draw it larger, so the open edge nearly touches the top corner and the handle points toward the bottom corner, filling most of the card height.

pairs.difference: B: the chest is in 3/4 view, with its right side close to the right edge and its planks running off the card. A: the suitcase faces straight on, centered and symmetrical, with an even gap on every side (margin 0.121, above the real range). That is the lessons' generated framing.
pairs.fix: Turn the suitcase to a three-quarter angle and draw it bigger, so one corner nearly touches the side edge and the floor runs off the bottom of the card.

pairs.difference: A: the piano fills a wide block of the card (area 0.395) against a plain striped wall. B: the guitar is narrow (width 0.523, below the real range) and covers only 0.169 of the card. Two spotlight beams, stage trusses on both sides and a bright floor glow compete with it, so at thumbnail size the stage reads before the guitar.
pairs.fix: Draw the guitar much larger at a diagonal tilt, filling most of the card. Make the background a simple soft stage glow with no truss towers and no strong light beams.

pairs.difference: A: the medal box is in 3/4 view, fills the card and sits close to the edges, like the real cards. B: the gate is a small part of a whole scene (area 0.157, margin 0.181), surrounded by brick pillars, hedges, a lawn and a paved path. This is the same thing as the generated lighthouse in the lessons, which added rocks and props. Here the setting outweighs the gate.
pairs.fix: Draw only the iron gate and its two pillars, large and filling the card. Turn them slightly to a three-quarter angle, and replace the garden, hedges and path with a simple background.

pairs.difference: A: the bugle bell pushes close to the top-left, and the body sweeps across the card on a diagonal (width 0.791). B: the violin is a thin, small diagonal in the middle of the rays (width 0.528, below the real range; area 0.146), with an even gap on every side (margin 0.119, above the real range).
pairs.fix: Draw the violin much larger, tilted across the card, so the scroll nearly touches the top-right corner and the body nearly reaches the bottom-left corner.

pattern: Generated cards show the whole object, small, centered and straight on, with an even gap on every side. Their margin_min is often above the real maximum of about 0.10–0.12. Flat, wide objects come out short (box_height under about 0.55) and leave empty background above and below. Sometimes the object sits inside an added scene (garden, stage trusses, tablecloth) that competes with it. Real cards draw the object bigger and tilted to a three-quarter angle, and let it come close to or run off at least one edge.
